checks_run: Inventoried and hashed the 52-file candidate tree and checked it for symlinks.
Inspected the requirements, learner guidance, manifest, provenance, validation record, exercises, tests, Makefiles, and complete reference C implementation.
Built the starter and sealed reference from clean state on a writable scratch copy with GCC 8.5.0.
Ran the submitted public, sealed boundary, direct API, adversarial, and repository-audit suites under outer timeouts.
Ran five independent CLI semantic and atomicity probes, an independent 500-case signed-arithmetic matrix, and an independently authored 18-check C API harness.
Probed embedded-NUL file handling, special-file handling, and valid deeply nested input.
Compiled all three C exercise fragments and ran an independent keyword-classifier probe.
Compared two clean same-host reference builds by SHA-256.
Checked internal manifest/provenance identifiers and hashes, license markers, progressive-disclosure layout, and validation-label honesty.
Attempted an AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer build.
evidence: The starter built cleanly; its test target exited 2 with 9 expected failures and 2 passes because the starter is explicitly a placeholder.
The reference clean build exited 0; 11 public tests, 18 sealed boundary tests, and 16 submitted API checks passed. The seven-test deterministic adversarial suite also passed.
Five independently chosen language/atomicity cases, 18 independent API checks, and all 500 arithmetic boundary combinations passed.
A valid 32,776-byte program with 16,384 nested parentheses died by SIGSEGV (return code -11), despite being far below the 1 MiB CLI limit.
A file containing `print 1;`, an embedded NUL, and `print 2;` exited 0 and printed only `1`, silently ignoring the trailing source; `/dev/null` was also accepted as an empty program.

The lexer debugging exercise correctly exposes short-prefix misclassification, but its claimed out-of-bounds read is not present: `strncmp(start, "let", length)` reads at most the supplied slice length and stops at NUL. The sealed answer repeats that incorrect safety claim.

The disclosure directory layout is sensible, but the submitted tree itself contains readable solutions, hidden tests, and the full reference, with no included student-view projector or transfer-verification evidence.
Manifest labels remain honestly limited to GENERATED and PARTIAL; the pack expressly disclaims fuzzing, benchmarking results, independent validation, transfer verification, and productionization.

Manifest, provenance, project, source, and commit identifiers are internally consistent. Two same-host clean reference builds produced the same executable SHA-256, 5dc3961e052a5aa3f71bd4ef5b938f736700c035d1c42b8fddfba27f6ce49de5.
The CC0 assertion is confined to catalog metadata and the linked tutorial is correctly marked NOASSERTION, but no redistribution license is granted for the generated challenge code and prose.
limitations: clang, valgrind, and ripgrep were unavailable. GCC sanitizer linking failed because libasan.so.5.0.0 and libubsan.so.1.0.0 were unavailable.
The upstream catalog and linked NOASSERTION tutorial were not available in scope, so source-license evidence, originality, and the no-copy assertion could not be independently verified.
No harness-generated learner view or transfer artifact was supplied, so progressive-disclosure isolation could be assessed structurally but not transfer-verified.
Rebuild comparison covered one GCC/Linux host and one path; no cross-compiler, cross-platform, concurrency, allocation-failure, or long-running load validation was possible.
Submitted suites and prose are recorded only as observations and do not establish BUILDS, TESTED, FUZZED, BENCHMARKED, REVIEWED, TRANSFER_VERIFIED, or PRODUCTIONIZED labels.
